intro: Days, months, seasons, and the small words that go with dates.
p.marzo.nota: The /θ/ guide is used in much of Spain; in seseante varieties, z sounds like /s/.
p.septiembre.nota: Setiembre is also a valid form.
p.el cumpleaños.nota: Singular, even with the final s.
b1.texto:
The week: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo.

The year: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre. In Spanish, weekdays, months and seasons are lowercase.

**¿Qué día es hoy?** usually asks for the day of the week. **¿Qué fecha es hoy?** asks for the calendar date.

For an event date, use **el** + number + **de** + month: **Mi cumpleaños es el tres de mayo**. When stating today's date after **ser**, the article is commonly omitted: **Hoy es doce de marzo**. The year follows **de**: **Mi cumpleaños es el 3 de mayo de 2025**. The first day is **el uno de enero**.

For a particular Monday, say **el lunes**; for every Monday, **los lunes**. Neither takes a preposition here.

Months, seasons and years take **en**: en agosto, en verano, en 2020. The dialogue follows Spain and the Northern Hemisphere. In countries with four seasons, summer and winter fall at opposite times of year across the hemispheres.
b3.f1: Today is Tuesday the twelfth of March.
b3.f3: On the third of August. It's always in summer.
b3.f4: My birthday is on the first of January, in winter.
b5.pregunta: Complete: my birthday is on 3 August.
b5.o1.refuerzo: En goes with months, seasons and years.
b5.o2.refuerzo: A goes with clock times: a las tres.
b6.pregunta: Complete: I always travel in summer.
b6.o1.refuerzo: El verano is the noun. In summer is en verano.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A is not used with seasons.
b7.pregunta: Which question asks for the full calendar date?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Fecha asks for the calendar date.
b7.o1.refuerzo: This asks for the day of the week.
b7.o2.refuerzo: This asks only which month it is.
b8.pregunta: Which date is written the Spanish way?
b8.o0.refuerzo: Day, then de, then the month, with no capital.
b8.o2.refuerzo: A date takes el, and months have no capital letter.
b9.pregunta: You work every Monday. Which sentence?
b9.o1.refuerzo: Days take el or los, not en.
b12.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (30–40 words).** Write today's date in full, your birthday and four important dates in your year.

**Speak (about 30 seconds).** Say aloud today's date, the birthdays in your family and what you do on each day of the week.
